```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

rm(list = ls())
```

## Purpose

The primary model (`fitmort_child_gen_krig_int`, the generalized kriging model with
`treatment × lat` and `treatment × lon` interactions) is fitted to all 1390 grappes.
Three districts — **Boboye**, **Falmey** and **Loga** — overlapped with the MORDOR mass
azithromycin trial, so their background mortality may have been depressed by prior mass
drug administration, and their treatment effect may be attenuated.

`mordor-question.qmd` approaches this by *adjusting*: adding a `mordorstate` indicator
and matching MORDOR villages. This document takes the complementary approach — it
*removes* the districts and refits, then asks whether the predicted mortality surfaces
and the ATE surface change in any way that would alter the conclusions:

1. **Excluding Boboye** — the largest of the three MORDOR districts
2. **Excluding Boboye, Falmey and Loga** — all three MORDOR-overlapping districts

Both refits use the primary specification unchanged, including the centred coordinates
introduced in `02A-spatial-models-fit.Rmd`, so the only difference is which grappes
enter the likelihood.

> **Interpretation caveat.** Predictions are generated over the *whole* `boxgrid`,
> including cells inside the dropped districts. In those cells the reduced models have
> no local data, so the Matérn field shrinks to zero and the prediction falls back to
> the fixed-effect plane. Those cells are flagged throughout and excluded from the
> quantitative comparisons — they show what the model extrapolates, not what it
> learned.

```{r load data}

source(here::here("analysis", "0-config.R"))
source(here::here("analysis", "0-functions.R"))

df_proj <- readRDS(here("data", "grappe_mortality_data.rds")) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = global_crs) %>%
  st_transform(crs = proj_crs) %>% # UTM zone 31N, for Niger
  mutate(lon = sf::st_coordinates(.)[, 1],
         lat = sf::st_coordinates(.)[, 2],
         isTreated_child_num = ifelse(isTreated_child == "Treatment", 1, 0))

boxgrid        <- readRDS(here("data", "boxgrid.rds"))
niger_adm2_sub <- readRDS(here("data", "niger_adm2_sub.rds"))

# The two exclusion sets, plus the full-data reference
excluded_districts <- list(
  full        = character(0),
  no_boboye   = "Boboye",
  no_mordor   = c("Boboye", "Falmey", "Loga")
)

variant_labels <- c(full      = "All districts",
                    no_boboye = "Excl. Boboye",
                    no_mordor = "Excl. Boboye, Falmey, Loga")

```

### What is being dropped

```{r data-loss-table}

df_proj %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(district) %>%
  summarise(n_grappe   = n(),
            n_treated  = sum(isTreated_child == "Treatment"),
            deaths     = sum(n_deaths_1to59),
            py         = round(sum(pt_year_1to59)),
            rate_1000  = round(1000 * sum(n_deaths_1to59) / sum(pt_year_1to59), 1),
            .groups    = "drop") %>%
  mutate(mordor_district = district %in% excluded_districts$no_mordor)

```

```{r data-loss-summary}

purrr::map_dfr(names(excluded_districts), function(v) {
  d <- df_proj %>% dplyr::filter(!district %in% excluded_districts[[v]])
  tibble(variant     = variant_labels[[v]],
         n_grappe    = nrow(d),
         n_treated   = sum(d$isTreated_child == "Treatment"),
         deaths      = sum(d$n_deaths_1to59),
         deaths_lost = sum(df_proj$n_deaths_1to59) - sum(d$n_deaths_1to59),
         pct_deaths_lost = round(100 * (1 - sum(d$n_deaths_1to59) /
                                          sum(df_proj$n_deaths_1to59)), 1))
})

```

## Refit the primary model on each subset

The formula is identical to `fitmort_child_gen_krig_int` in `02A-spatial-models-fit.Rmd`
— centred coordinates in km, Matérn field on the uncentred metre coordinates, Poisson
with a `log(pt_year_1to59)` offset, fitted by ML. The full-data fit is *loaded*, not
refitted, so it is guaranteed to be the same object the rest of the repo uses.

Controlled by `refit_exclusion_models_flag` in `0-config.R`. Each refit takes roughly
4–5 minutes with `r avail_thr` threads.

```{r fit-exclusion-models}

fit_paths <- c(full      = here("data", "fitmort_child_gen_krig_int.rds"),
               no_boboye = here("data", "fitmort_child_gen_krig_int_no_boboye.rds"),
               no_mordor = here("data", "fitmort_child_gen_krig_int_no_mordor.rds"))

if(refit_exclusion_models_flag) {

  for(v in c("no_boboye", "no_mordor")) {

    dat_v <- df_proj %>% dplyr::filter(!district %in% excluded_districts[[v]])

    tic(paste("Refit primary model,", variant_labels[[v]]))
    fit_v <- spaMM::fitme(
      n_deaths_1to59 ~
        1 +
        I((lat - 1448231) / 1000) + I((lon - 552981) / 1000) +
        Matern(1 | lon + lat) +
        isTreated_child +
        isTreated_child:I((lat - 1448231) / 1000) +
        isTreated_child:I((lon -  552981) / 1000) +
        offset(log(pt_year_1to59)),
      data = dat_v,
      family = poisson(link = "log"),
      control.HLfit = list(NbThreads = avail_thr)
    )
    toc()

    saveRDS(fit_v, fit_paths[[v]])
  }
}

fits <- purrr::map(fit_paths, readRDS)

# All three must be the same specification, or the comparison is meaningless
stopifnot(all(purrr::map_int(fits, ~ length(fixef(.x))) == 6))

```

## Coefficients and variance components

```{r coefficient-table}

purrr::imap_dfr(fits, function(f, v) {
  b  <- fixef(f)
  se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(f)))
  cp <- f$CorrEst_and_RanFix$corrPars$`1`
  tibble(
    variant   = variant_labels[[v]],
    n_grappe  = length(fitted(f)),
    term      = names(b) %>%
      str_replace(fixed("I((lat - 1448231)/1000)"), "lat_c") %>%
      str_replace(fixed("I((lon - 552981)/1000)"), "lon_c") %>%
      str_replace("isTreated_childTreatment", "Trt"),
    estimate  = as.numeric(b),
    se        = as.numeric(se),
    t         = as.numeric(b / se)
  )
}) %>%
  mutate(across(c(estimate, se, t), ~ signif(.x, 3))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = term, names_from = variant,
                     values_from = c(estimate, se, t))

```

`Trt` is the log rate ratio **at the grappe centroid** (coordinates are centred), and
`Trt:lat_c` / `Trt:lon_c` are the per-km gradients in that log rate ratio.

```{r variance-components}

purrr::imap_dfr(fits, function(f, v) {
  cp <- f$CorrEst_and_RanFix$corrPars$`1`
  tibble(variant  = variant_labels[[v]],
         n_grappe = length(fitted(f)),
         nu       = signif(cp$nu, 4),
         rho      = signif(cp$rho, 4),
         range_km = signif(1 / (1000 * cp$rho), 4),
         lambda   = signif(f$lambda[[1]], 4),
         logLik   = signif(as.numeric(logLik(f, which = "p_v")), 6),
         AIC      = signif(AIC(f)[1], 6))
})

```

AIC and logLik are **not** comparable across rows — the three models are fitted to
different numbers of observations. They are reported only to document each fit.

## Predicted surfaces

```{r grid-predictions}

# One prediction surface per variant per arm, over the full boxgrid
preds_long <- purrr::imap_dfr(fits, function(f, v) {
  get_grid_preds_both_tx(input_grid = boxgrid, spamm_model_fit = f) %>%
    mutate(variant = variant_labels[[v]])
})

preds_wide <- preds_long %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = c(variant, district, geometry),
                     names_from = isTreated_child,
                     values_from = pred, names_prefix = "pred") %>%
  mutate(ATE        = predTreatment - predControl,
         rate_ratio = predTreatment / predControl,
         # cells the reduced models never saw data in
         dropped_boboye = district %in% excluded_districts$no_boboye,
         dropped_mordor = district %in% excluded_districts$no_mordor) %>%
  mutate(variant = factor(variant, levels = unname(variant_labels)))

```

```{r base-map}

base_map <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        axis.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 7))

# outline of the districts dropped in each scenario, for overlay
boboye_outline <- niger_adm2_sub %>%
  dplyr::filter(adm2_name %in% excluded_districts$no_boboye)
mordor_outline <- niger_adm2_sub %>%
  dplyr::filter(adm2_name %in% excluded_districts$no_mordor)

```

### Mortality surfaces, both arms

```{r mortality-surfaces}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8

mort_df <- preds_long %>%
  mutate(variant = factor(variant, levels = unname(variant_labels))) %>%
  group_by(variant, isTreated_child) %>%
  group_split()

mort_keys <- preds_long %>%
  mutate(variant = factor(variant, levels = unname(variant_labels))) %>%
  group_by(variant, isTreated_child) %>%
  group_keys()

mort_rast <- purrr::map(mort_df, ~ make_raster_map(.x, proj_crs, global_crs, "pred"))
names(mort_rast) <- paste(mort_keys$variant, mort_keys$isTreated_child, sep = "__")

mort_raster_df <- purrr::imap_dfr(mort_rast, function(res, name) {
  parts <- strsplit(name, "__")[[1]]
  as.data.frame(res, xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(variant = parts[1], arm = parts[2])
}) %>%
  mutate(variant = factor(variant, levels = unname(variant_labels)))

p_mort <- base_map +
  geom_raster(data = mort_raster_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = pred), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = mordor_outline, fill = NA, color = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_grid(arm ~ variant) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "Predicted deaths / 1000 py",
                       guide = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top")) +
  labs(caption = "Red outline: the three MORDOR-overlapping districts.")

p_mort

```

### ATE surfaces

```{r ate-surfaces}
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.5

ate_df   <- preds_wide %>% group_by(variant) %>% group_split()
ate_keys <- preds_wide %>% group_by(variant) %>% group_keys()

ate_rast <- purrr::map(ate_df, ~ make_raster_map(.x, proj_crs, global_crs, "ATE"))
names(ate_rast) <- as.character(ate_keys$variant)

ate_raster_df <- purrr::imap_dfr(ate_rast, function(res, name) {
  as.data.frame(res, xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE) %>% mutate(variant = name)
}) %>%
  mutate(variant = factor(variant, levels = unname(variant_labels)))

p_ate <- base_map +
  geom_raster(data = ate_raster_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = ATE), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = mordor_outline, fill = NA, color = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ variant) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(name = "ATE (deaths / 1000 py)",
                       low = "#2166ac", mid = "white", high = "#b2182b",
                       midpoint = 0,
                       # wide bar + explicit breaks: the default is too narrow here
                       # and the tick labels overprint each other
                       breaks = seq(-10, 2, by = 2),
                       guide = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top",
                                              barwidth = unit(9, "cm"))) +
  labs(caption = "Negative (blue) = treatment arm has lower predicted mortality.")

p_ate

```

### How far does the ATE surface move?

```{r ate-difference-maps}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.5

ate_diff <- preds_wide %>%
  sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::select(variant, ATE) %>%
  mutate(cell = rep(seq_len(nrow(boxgrid)), times = length(fits))) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = cell, names_from = variant, values_from = ATE)

names(ate_diff) <- c("cell", "full", "no_boboye", "no_mordor")

diff_sf <- boxgrid %>%
  mutate(diff_boboye = ate_diff$no_boboye - ate_diff$full,
         diff_mordor = ate_diff$no_mordor - ate_diff$full)

# factor(), not character: group_split()/facet_wrap() would otherwise order these
# alphabetically and put the three-district comparison first
diff_levels <- c("Excl. Boboye", "Excl. Boboye, Falmey, Loga")

diff_long <- bind_rows(
  diff_sf %>% mutate(pred = diff_boboye, comparison = diff_levels[1]),
  diff_sf %>% mutate(pred = diff_mordor, comparison = diff_levels[2])
) %>%
  mutate(comparison = factor(comparison, levels = diff_levels))

diff_split <- diff_long %>% group_by(comparison) %>% group_split()
diff_keys  <- diff_long %>% group_by(comparison) %>% group_keys()
diff_rast  <- purrr::map(diff_split, ~ make_raster_map(.x, proj_crs, global_crs, "pred"))
names(diff_rast) <- diff_keys$comparison

diff_raster_df <- purrr::imap_dfr(diff_rast, function(res, name) {
  as.data.frame(res, xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE) %>% mutate(comparison = name)
}) %>%
  mutate(comparison = factor(comparison, levels = diff_levels))

p_diff <- base_map +
  geom_raster(data = diff_raster_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = pred), na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_sf(data = niger_adm2_sub, fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = mordor_outline, fill = NA, color = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ comparison) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(name = "Change in ATE (deaths / 1000 py)",
                       low = "#4d9221", mid = "white", high = "#c51b7d",
                       midpoint = 0,
                       guide = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top",
                                              barwidth = unit(9, "cm"))) +
  labs(caption = paste("Change relative to the full-data fit.",
                       "Green = more protective without those districts.",
                       "\nCells inside the red outline are extrapolations."))

p_diff

```

### Cell-by-cell agreement

```{r ate-scatter}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.5

scatter_dat <- bind_rows(
  tibble(full = ate_diff$full, excluded = ate_diff$no_boboye,
         comparison = "Excl. Boboye",
         in_dropped = boxgrid$district %in% excluded_districts$no_boboye),
  tibble(full = ate_diff$full, excluded = ate_diff$no_mordor,
         comparison = "Excl. Boboye, Falmey, Loga",
         in_dropped = boxgrid$district %in% excluded_districts$no_mordor)
)

p_scatter <- ggplot(scatter_dat, aes(x = full, y = excluded, color = in_dropped)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  geom_point(size = 0.3, alpha = 0.3) +
  ggpubr::stat_cor(data = scatter_dat %>% dplyr::filter(!in_dropped),
                   aes(x = full, y = excluded), inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ comparison) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Grid cell is in a dropped district",
                     values = c(`FALSE` = "#2166ac", `TRUE` = "#b2182b")) +
  labs(x = "ATE, all districts (deaths / 1000 py)",
       y = "ATE, reduced fit") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

p_scatter

```

The correlation reported is computed on **retained** cells only.

```{r ate-agreement-table}

purrr::map_dfr(c("no_boboye", "no_mordor"), function(v) {
  keep <- !boxgrid$district %in% excluded_districts[[v]]
  d    <- ate_diff[[v]] - ate_diff$full
  tibble(
    variant          = variant_labels[[v]],
    cells_retained   = sum(keep),
    cells_dropped    = sum(!keep),
    cor_retained     = round(cor(ate_diff$full[keep], ate_diff[[v]][keep]), 4),
    mean_abs_diff    = round(mean(abs(d[keep])), 3),
    max_abs_diff     = round(max(abs(d[keep])), 3),
    ate_min_retained = round(min(ate_diff[[v]][keep]), 2),
    ate_max_retained = round(max(ate_diff[[v]][keep]), 2),
    ate_min_full     = round(min(ate_diff$full[keep]), 2),
    ate_max_full     = round(max(ate_diff$full[keep]), 2)
  )
})

```

```{r save-outputs}

saveRDS(preds_wide, here("data", "preds_ATE_district_exclusion.rds"))

```

## Findings

**The average treatment effect survives; the *spatial gradient* in it does not.**

The treatment effect at the study centroid is stable and, if anything, strengthens as
the MORDOR districts are removed — log RR −0.180 (RR 0.84, t = −4.12) on all districts,
−0.205 (RR 0.81, t = −4.22) without Boboye, −0.237 (RR 0.79, t = −3.54) without all
three. It stays significant in every fit despite losing 31% of the deaths in the
largest exclusion. The direction is what a MORDOR-attenuation story predicts: the
districts with prior mass drug administration were diluting the overall effect.

The east–west interaction behaves very differently:

| fit | `Trt:lon_c` | SE | t |
|---|---|---|---|
| All districts | −0.00283 | 0.00100 | **−2.83** |
| Excl. Boboye | −0.00209 | 0.00131 | −1.60 |
| Excl. Boboye, Falmey, Loga | −0.00098 | 0.00180 | −0.55 |

The point estimate falls by 65% while the SE inflates by 1.8×, so this is not only a
power loss — the coefficient itself moves far more than dropping 31% of events would
explain. The north–south interaction, never significant, collapses similarly
(t = 1.46 → 0.98 → 0.22).

**Why: the harmful corner of the ATE surface is Boboye.** In the full-data fit, of the
1464 grid cells with a positive (harmful) ATE, 1223 are in Boboye, 217 in Falmey and 15
in Loga — 99.4% of them inside MORDOR districts, and 75.8% of Boboye's cells are
positive. Boboye and Falmey are also the two westernmost districts (mean longitude
2.87°E and 2.86°E, against 3.37–4.11°E for the rest). The significant east–west
gradient is therefore anchored by a near-null-to-harmful estimate at the western edge;
remove that edge and the gradient has little left to stand on.

Consistent with this, both reduced fits predict a **uniformly protective** surface over
the districts they retain: ATE spans −10.60 to −0.37 without Boboye and −9.34 to −1.39
without all three, against −11.12 to +0.88 for the full fit over the same cells. No
harmful pocket remains anywhere.

**Elsewhere the surface barely moves.** Over retained cells the ATE correlates with the
full-data surface at 0.983 (excl. Boboye; mean absolute change 0.30 deaths per 1000 py,
max 1.43) and 0.899 (excl. all three; mean 0.56, max 2.13). The difference maps show the
change concentrated in and around the dropped districts, shading green — more protective
— as the attenuating districts leave, with the far south-east drifting very slightly the
other way.

**Inside the dropped districts the models extrapolate, as expected.** Without Boboye,
the predicted ATE there swings from the full fit's −0.89 … +2.35 to −1.40 … +0.39: the
harmful signal in Boboye was coming from Boboye's own data, and once that data is gone
the model fills the hole with the regional plane. Those cells are diagnostic, not
estimates.

**The Matérn range shortens** — 11.4 km → 9.4 km → 8.2 km — with `nu` rising from 0.234
to 0.368. Some of this is genuinely less data over a smaller, less contiguous footprint,
so it should not be read as evidence about MORDOR.

### What this means for the primary analysis

The ATE itself is robust. The claim that the treatment effect *varies systematically
across space* — the east–west gradient in `fitmort_child_gen_krig_int` — is not robust
to excluding the MORDOR-overlapping districts, because those districts supply the
western, weakest-effect end of the gradient. That is not the same as saying the gradient
is an artefact: prior mass azithromycin administration is a plausible *reason* for a
genuinely weaker effect there, and dropping the districts removes the contrast that
identifies it. But any statement about spatial heterogeneity in the ATE should be
reported alongside this sensitivity analysis, and the covariate-adjustment results in
`mordor-question.qmd` read as the complementary evidence.
